chapter_note: Heavily damaged chapter (73.7% damage ratio) but the core teaching about the cloud — its origin from the place of fire/heaven against the Virgin of Light, the cycle of archons and angels, the fossae outside the great sea, and the role of the Omophoros — is unmistakably cosmological substrate. The dialogue frame opens (segs 0-9) with question and pedagogical bridge; closes (segs 116-132) with hortatory recapitulation ('I have made known to you... I have also taught you...') and disciples' doxology. The substantive cosmological question 'What is a cloud?' is preserved as substrate content. A second embedded question about where the seven fossae descend (91-92) likewise preserves substrate content. The Omophoros answer (96) and the archon-disguise teaching (98ff) continue cosmological substrate. Editorial fatigue is mild; substrate vocabulary actually rises in the second half.
